verification.scope: Beginner suitability and structural validation for 600 sentences; sentence pinyin and English added in v1.6.0. Examples/translations are not individually corpus-attested or native-speaker certified.
verification.word_id_source: Entry IDs 1–300 are carried over unchanged from the supplied v1.3.0 dataset. This export does NOT independently certify that these numbers match the November 2025 official syllabus serial numbers.
verification.conversational_examples: 300 original conversational examples retained except targeted corrections for naturalness and beginner vocabulary.
verification.written_examples: Most second examples replaced with short everyday descriptions, classroom instructions, or written dialogue, instead of advanced/literary formal language.
verification.register_policy: written=plain written descriptions or classroom notices, not high-register Chinese. Spoken particles and greetings appear in written dialogue when formal prose would be unnatural.
verification.difficulty_policy: Prefer HSK 3.0 2025 Level 1; allow common Level 2 vocabulary and grammar. Transparent compounds and proper names may be present. No Level 3 把 disposal construction or chair classifier, 需要, 应该, 如果.
verification.translation_and_pinyin: 300 headword meanings come directly from the original XLSX-derived v1.1.0 dataset. For sentences unchanged from original XLSX, pinyin and English are reused from the original. For rewritten/new sentences, pinyin and translations are editorial enrichments (using ICU Han-Latin lexicon with curated lexical readings and sandhi), not independently native-speaker certified; manual review is recommended.
verification.vocabulary_boundary_policy: Hard ceiling: November 2025 HSK 3.0 Level 2 cumulative vocabulary (IDs 1–500). Level 1 examples may use Level 2 items; Level 3+ standalone vocabulary is not intentionally introduced. Normal grammar particles and contracted negative 没 (short form of 没有) are allowed; orthographic parts inside a listed word are not treated as separate unlisted vocabulary. Original lexical lists do not encode every compositional collocation. Independent linguistic/native-speaker verification has not been performed.
verification.vocabulary_boundary_audit: A vocabulary-token segmentation screen was applied to 100% of example sentences; all characters in Hanzi sentences are covered by Level 1/2 headwords, except standalone 没 (a grammatically licensed short form of 没有). This is a segmentation heuristic, not a conclusive proof of lexical or grammar-level compliance. This statement describes the earlier vocabulary screen and does not cover the v1.7.1 revisions.
verification.sentence_revision: v1.7.1: Applied the supplied register and naturalness patch to 33 sentences across 32 Level 1 entries. Updated pinyin, translations, notes and register for those examples. ID 127 uses the non-erhua written counterpart of the headword. Vocabulary compliance of the revised sentences was not independently verified.

examples.note: 爱 expresses strong affection here; 家 can refer both to the home and to one’s family.
examples.english: I love my family.

examples.note: School or study context showing 爱 in a simple description.
examples.english: Dad loves watching Chinese-language movies.

examples.note: 八 gives the quantity; 本 is the classifier used for bound books.
examples.english: I have eight books.

examples.note: School or study context showing 八 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: jīntiān yǒu bā gè xuéshēng shàngkè.
examples.english: Eight students have class today.

examples.note: 爸爸 is a familiar kinship noun, and the possessive 的 is often omitted before close family terms.
examples.english: My father is a teacher.

examples.note: Family or daily-life description using 爸爸 without advanced grammar.
examples.english: Dad is cooking at home.

examples.note: Sentence-final 吧 softens a proposal into a friendly suggestion to go together.
examples.english: Let's go.

examples.note: Written dialogue: 吧 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: "Come back tomorrow," the teacher said.

entries.pos_note: Sentence-final suggestion or softening particle.

examples.note: 白天 contrasts with 晚上 and places the work in daytime hours.
examples.english: I work during the day.

examples.note: The time word comes before the phrase that says where the students study.
examples.english: The students study at school during the day.

examples.note: 一百 means one hundred; 个 is the general classifier for people here.
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ yǒu yì bǎi ge rén.
examples.english: There are a hundred people here.

examples.hanzi: 这家书店有一百本中文书。
examples.note: School or study context showing 百 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā shūdiàn yǒu yì bǎi běn Zhōngwén shū.
examples.english: This bookstore has one hundred books in Chinese.

examples.note: 八点半 is the ordinary way to say 8:30; 半 means half an hour.
examples.english: It is half past eight now.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 半 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào shàngwǔ bā diǎn bàn shàngkè.
examples.english: Classes at the school start at 8:30 a.m.

entries.pos_note: Primarily the numeral “half” (半个小时, 八点半). Also has a restricted adverbial role meaning partly/half- in advanced patterns; that secondary role is not a Level 1 teaching priority.

examples.note: 包子 is a filled steamed bun; 早上 sets the morning time frame.
examples.english: I eat steamed buns in the morning.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 包子.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā diàn de bāozi hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The steamed buns at this shop are delicious.

examples.note: The final 我的 stands for “my cup,” with the repeated noun left understood.
examples.english: This cup is mine.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 杯子 in context.
examples.pinyin: zhuōzi shàng yǒu sān gè bēizi.
examples.english: There are three cups on the table.

examples.note: 本 is the standard classifier for books; 两 normally precedes classifiers rather than 二.
examples.pinyin: wǒ mǎi le liǎng běn shū.
examples.english: I bought two books.

examples.note: School or study context showing 本 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéshēng měi rén yǒu yì běn shū.
examples.english: Every student has one book.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 边 in context.
examples.english: Come sit over here.

examples.note: School or study context showing 边 in a simple description.
examples.english: The school is over there.

entries.pos_note: Primarily a bound locative suffix in 这边、那边、前边; also a noun meaning side or edge in other constructions.

examples.note: 生病 is the ordinary way to say someone is ill; 有病 can sound judgmental in conversation.
examples.english: He is ill.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 病 in context.
examples.english: His illness has gotten better.

entries.pos_note: Illness as a noun; also occurs in verbal uses.

examples.note: 不 negates a general action or preference; there is no aspect marker for a habitual statement.
examples.english: I do not drink tea.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 不.
examples.english: Tea is not sold here.

examples.note: 不客气 is a standard spoken response to thanks; the short answer is a complete utterance.
examples.english: You're welcome!

examples.note: Written dialogue: 不客气 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: She said, "You're welcome."

entries.pos_note: Conventional response to thanks; classify as a fixed expression, not by the characters separately.

examples.note: 不要 directly rejects an offered object; in some contexts it can sound firm.
examples.english: I don't want this one.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 不要; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.pinyin: qǐng búyào zài zhèlǐ chī dōngxi.
examples.english: Please don't eat here.

entries.pos_note: Negative request/prohibition: 不 + 要; an expression rather than a single lexical category.

examples.note: 菜 usually refers to a prepared dish here, and 好吃 describes how it tastes.
examples.english: This dish is delicious.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 菜.
examples.pinyin: fàndiàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō cài.
examples.english: There are many dishes at the restaurant.

examples.note: 喜欢 + verb expresses an enjoyable activity; 喝茶 is “drink tea.”
examples.english: I like drinking tea.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 茶.
examples.english: This shop sells tea.

examples.note: 会 marks learned ability; 中文歌 means songs sung in Chinese.
examples.english: She can sing songs in Chinese.

examples.note: School or study context showing 唱 in a simple description.

examples.note: 去 + place + verb expresses going somewhere in order to do something.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 超市 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The supermarket opens at eight in the morning.

examples.note: Family or daily-life description using 车 without advanced grammar.
examples.pinyin: zhè shì wǒ bàba de chē.
examples.english: This is my dad's car.

examples.note: School or study context showing 车 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào ménkǒu yǒu hěn duō chē.
examples.english: There are many cars at the school entrance.

examples.note: 一起 emphasizes a shared activity; 吃饭 can mean having a meal in general.
examples.english: We eat together.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 吃; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.pinyin: qǐng zài shí èr diǎn chī wǔfàn.
examples.english: Please have lunch at twelve o'clock.

examples.note: 坐出租车 means travel by taxi, rather than literally sit in a taxi.
examples.english: I take a taxi to school.

examples.pinyin: cóng xuéxiào dào yīyuàn kěyǐ zuò chūzūchē.
examples.english: You can take a taxi from the school to the hospital.

examples.note: 穿 refers to wearing clothes; Chinese does not need a progressive form for the current outfit.
examples.english: I am wearing new clothes today.

examples.hanzi: 天气冷的时候，请多穿衣服。
examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 穿; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.pinyin: tiānqì lěng de shíhou, qǐng duō chuān yīfu.
examples.english: When it is cold, please wear more clothes.

examples.note: 给妈妈 identifies the recipient of the phone call; 打电话 is a verb-object expression.

examples.english: I want to call my mother.

examples.hanzi: 请明天上午给老师打电话。

examples.pinyin: qǐng míngtiān shàngwǔ gěi lǎoshī dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Please call the teacher tomorrow morning.

examples.note: 很 appears naturally before a descriptive adjective such as 大, without necessarily meaning “very.”
examples.english: This room is big.

examples.english: This university is very big.

examples.note: 大家 refers to everyone present or in the relevant group; 都 reinforces “all.”

examples.pinyin: dàxué lǐ yǒu hěn duō xuéshēng.

examples.english: She is a university student.

examples.hanzi: 大学生也可以在这里读书。
examples.note: School or study context showing 大学生 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: dàxuéshēng yě kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ dúshū.

examples.note: School or study context showing 到 in a simple description.

examples.english: This is my book.

examples.english: Dad's car is over there.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 第 in context.

examples.note: Family or daily-life description using 弟弟 without advanced grammar.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 点 in a straightforward sentence.

examples.note: 家 can classify a shop or commercial establishment; 很小 describes its size.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 店 in a straightforward sentence.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 电话; the tone is polite or neutral.

examples.note: School or study context showing 电话 in a simple description.
examples.english: This is the school's phone number.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 电脑 in context.
examples.english: I study on the computer.

examples.note: School or study context showing 电脑 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào lǐ yǒu hěn duō diànnǎo.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 电影 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: Shall we watch a movie tonight?

examples.english: There is a new movie at the cinema today.

examples.english: We are all students.

examples.note: School or study context showing 都 in a simple description.
examples.english: All the students are in the classroom.

examples.english: I can read Chinese characters.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 读; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.english: Please read this lesson.

examples.english: I read books every day.

examples.hanzi: 学生们每天在学校读书。
examples.note: School or study context showing 读书 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students read at school every day.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 对 in context.
examples.english: Am I right?

examples.note: Written dialogue: 对 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: The teacher said, "Yes, that's right."

examples.pinyin: xiàwǔ lái de rén hěn duō.
examples.english: There are many people coming this afternoon.

examples.english: How much does this cost?

examples.english: How many students are in this class?

examples.note: 儿子 specifies one’s son; 喜欢 is followed by the thing liked.

examples.pinyin: tā de érzi jīnnián shàng xiǎoxué.
examples.english: His son is attending primary school this year.

examples.note: 二十 is the number twenty; 本 counts books.
examples.english: I have twenty books.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 二 in context.
examples.pinyin: jīntiān shì èr yuè èr rì.
examples.english: Today is February 2.

examples.english: Today’s meal tastes delicious.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 饭.
examples.english: The family eats dinner together.

examples.pinyin: zhè jiā fàndiàn měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn kāimén.

examples.english: My room is small.

examples.pinyin: xuéxiào lǐ yǒu sān gè dà fángjiān.
examples.english: There are three large rooms at the school.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 非常.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 好.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā fàndiàn de cài hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is very good.

examples.note: 好吃 evaluates the taste of food, not its appearance.
examples.english: This apple tastes good.

examples.hanzi: 这家饭店的面条很好吃。
examples.note: The adjective describes how the noodles taste.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā fàndiàn de miàntiáo hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The noodles at this restaurant are delicious.

examples.note: 件 is a classifier for clothing; 好看 describes how the garment looks.
examples.english: This item of clothing looks nice.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 好看 in context.
examples.english: This book is very good to read.

examples.note: School or study context showing 好听 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: wǒ juéde Zhōngwén gē hěn hǎotīng.
examples.english: I think Chinese songs sound really nice.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 好听 in context.
examples.pinyin: tā chàng de gē hěn hǎotīng.
examples.english: The songs she sings sound very nice.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 好玩儿 in context.
examples.english: It's really fun here!

examples.hanzi: “这里有很多好玩儿的东西。”小朋友说。
examples.note: The original spoken form fits naturally in quoted dialogue.
examples.pinyin: “zhèlǐ yǒu hěn duō hǎowánr de dōngxi.” xiǎopéngyǒu shuō.
examples.english: “There are lots of fun things here,” the child said.

examples.note: 号 is a common spoken way to state a day of the month; 月 identifies the month.
examples.pinyin: jīntiān shì shí yuè shísì hào.
examples.english: Today is October 14.

examples.hanzi: 老师说：“十月五号不上课。”
examples.note: The day of the month uses hào in the teacher’s speech.
examples.pinyin: lǎoshī shuō: “shí yuè wǔ hào bú shàngkè.”
examples.english: The teacher said, “There’s no class on October 5.”

examples.note: 想 + verb expresses a wish; 想喝 is wanting to drink.
examples.english: I want to drink water.

examples.note: School or study context showing 喝 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students drink water every day.

examples.note: 和 joins two people; 一起 clarifies that they go together.
examples.english: I will go with you.

examples.note: School or study context showing 和 in a simple description.
examples.english: We study together with the teacher.

entries.pos_note: Connects nouns and nominal phrases as and; with is a prepositional use.

examples.note: 很 often functions as a natural degree linker before adjectives, not an emphatic “very.”
examples.english: He is very happy.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 很.
examples.english: This shop is very big.

examples.note: 后边 is a positional noun meaning behind; 在 + person + 后边 locates the speaker.
examples.english: I am sitting behind you.

examples.note: School or study context showing 后 in a simple description.
examples.english: We go to the bookstore after class.

entries.pos_note: After/behind: temporal or spatial localizer; can also be nominal.

examples.note: 回家 means return home; 明天 indicates the future without a future-tense ending.
examples.english: I will go home tomorrow.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 回 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: tā xiàwǔ liù diǎn huí jiā.
examples.english: He goes home at six in the afternoon.

examples.note: 会 refers to an acquired skill, such as speaking a language.
examples.english: I can speak Chinese.

examples.note: The modal expresses a learned skill.
examples.pinyin: tā huì xiě hěn duō hànzì.
examples.english: She can write many Chinese characters.

entries.pos_note: Modal use for learned ability; the full word has other uses.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: wǒ zuò huǒchē qù kàn péngyou.
examples.english: I take the train to visit a friend.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 火车 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The train arrives at nine in the morning.

examples.note: 早饭 establishes the meal; 吃鸡蛋 names the food eaten.
examples.english: I eat eggs for breakfast.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 鸡蛋.
examples.english: There are eggs for breakfast today.

examples.note: 几 asks “how many” for a relatively small count and is followed by a classifier.
examples.english: How many friends do you have?

examples.note: School or study context showing 几 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: jīntiān lái le jǐ gè xuéshēng?
examples.english: How many students came today?

entries.pos_note: Interrogative quantity pronoun/numeral meaning how many (几个人、几本书). 个 or 本 is the classifier; 几 is NOT a classifier.

examples.note: 回家 means go back home, with no need for 在 before 家.
examples.english: I am going home now.

examples.note: Here the target word refers to the place where he lives.
examples.pinyin: tā de jiā zài xuéxiào pángbiān.
examples.english: His home is next to the school.

entries.pos_note: Home/family noun; also a classifier for businesses/families.

examples.note: 家人 refers to family members; 都 confirms that the whole group is doing well.
examples.pinyin: wǒ de jiārén dōu hěn hǎo.
examples.english: My family members are all well.

examples.hanzi: 星期天，他和家人一起去超市买东西。
examples.note: The target word means family members collectively.
examples.pinyin: xīngqītiān, tā hé jiārén yìqǐ qù chāoshì mǎi dōngxi.
examples.english: On Sunday, he went shopping at the supermarket with his family.

examples.note: 明天见 is a short, common parting expression meaning “see you tomorrow.”
examples.english: See you tomorrow!

examples.note: Written dialogue: 见 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: "See you on Monday!" she said.

examples.note: 件 is the measure word for individual items of clothing.
examples.pinyin: wǒ mǎi le yí jiàn yīfu.
examples.english: I bought an item of clothing.

examples.hanzi: 商店里有一件很漂亮的衣服。
examples.note: The classifier counts an individual garment.
examples.pinyin: shāngdiàn lǐ yǒu yí jiàn hěn piàoliang de yīfu.
examples.english: There is a very pretty piece of clothing in the shop.

examples.note: 饺子 are dumplings; 喜欢吃 specifies enjoyment of eating them.
examples.english: I like eating dumplings.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 饺子.
examples.english: This restaurant sells dumplings.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.english: What is your name?

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.english: The children call her Mom.

examples.note: 会开车 indicates the learned ability to drive.
examples.english: My older sister can drive.

examples.hanzi: 姐姐每天上午八点去公司上班。
examples.note: The family term can stand on its own when the relationship is understood.
examples.pinyin: jiějie měitiān shàngwǔ bā diǎn qù gōngsī shàngbān.
examples.english: My older sister goes to work at the office at eight every morning.

examples.note: 今年 sets the time frame; 在学 marks learning in progress, rather than a finished action.
examples.english: I'm studying Chinese this year.

examples.hanzi: 今年学校有很多新学生。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 今年 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: jīnnián xuéxiào yǒu hěn duō xīn xuéshēng.
examples.english: There are many new students at the school this year.

examples.note: 今天 marks the current day; 汉语课 means Chinese-language class.
examples.english: I have Chinese class today.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 今天 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: We don't have class this afternoon.

examples.note: 个 is the general classifier used when counting apples.
examples.english: I have nine apples.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 九 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: Classes at the school start at nine o'clock.

examples.note: 觉得 introduces a personal opinion or impression.
examples.english: I think this is good.

examples.note: School or study context showing 觉得 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéshēng juéde zhè běn shū hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The students think this book is good.

examples.note: 请 softens the imperative; 开门 means open the door.
examples.english: Please open the door.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 开 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The shop opens at eight in the morning.

examples.note: 会 marks the skill of driving rather than permission to drive.
examples.english: My father can drive.

examples.note: Family or daily-life description using 开车 without advanced grammar.
examples.english: Dad drives to the company today.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 看 in context.
examples.pinyin: nǐ kàn, zhè běn shū hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Look, this book is very good.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 看; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.pinyin: qǐng kàn zhè běn Zhōngwén shū.
examples.english: Please look at this Chinese book.

examples.note: 看病 means consult a doctor or seek medical care, not merely “look at illness.”
examples.pinyin: wǒ shēngbìng le, yào qù kànbìng.
examples.english: I am sick and need to see a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 医生上午九点开始看病。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 看病 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: yīshēng shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ kànbìng.
examples.english: The doctor starts seeing patients at nine in the morning.

examples.note: 看见 emphasizes successful visual perception; here the speaker spots a cat.
examples.english: I see a cat.

examples.note: School or study context showing 看见 in a simple description.
examples.english: You can see the school from here.

examples.note: 可以…吗 requests permission. 坐这儿 is natural colloquial Mandarin; 坐在这里 is an alternative.
examples.english: May I sit here?

examples.hanzi: 这里可以看书，也可以休息。
examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 可以 in context.
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ kěyǐ kàn shū, yě kěyǐ xiūxi.
examples.english: You can read books and rest here.

entries.pos_note: Modal/verb expressing permission or possibility; some lexical sources also label adjectival use.

examples.note: 课 is a class or lesson; 有 + noun expresses having a scheduled class.
examples.english: We have Chinese class in the morning.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 课 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The school has no classes on Sundays.

examples.note: 口 acts as a measure word for a sip or mouthful, not the noun “mouth” here.
examples.pinyin: wǒ hē le yì kǒu shuǐ.
examples.english: I took a sip of water.

examples.hanzi: 天气很热，他回家后喝了三口水。
examples.note: The measure word counts mouthfuls of water.
examples.pinyin: tiānqì hěn rè, tā huí jiā hòu hē le sān kǒu shuǐ.
examples.english: It was hot. After he got home, he took three sips of water.

entries.pos_note: Noun for mouth; also classifier in expressions such as population count.

examples.note: 块钱 is a common spoken expression for an amount in yuan.
examples.english: This apple costs five yuan.

examples.note: The everyday currency unit appears in quoted speech.
examples.pinyin: “zhè běn shū èrshí kuài qián.” tā shuō.
examples.english: “This book costs twenty yuan,” she said.

entries.pos_note: Classifier and colloquial monetary unit; also used for pieces.

examples.note: 来 indicates movement toward the speaker’s place or point of reference.
examples.english: Are you coming tomorrow?

examples.hanzi: 学生们明天上午来学校。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 来 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The students will come to school tomorrow morning.

examples.note: 老师 denotes a teacher; 我们的 specifies the group’s teacher.
examples.english: Our teacher is very good.

examples.note: School or study context showing 老师 in a simple description.
examples.english: The teacher is in the classroom.

examples.note: 了 after 吃 marks a completed event, not a past-tense conjugation.
examples.pinyin: wǒ chī le yí ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: I ate an apple.

examples.hanzi: 现在八点半了，学生们已经开始上课了。
examples.note: Both clause endings mark an update to the situation.
examples.pinyin: xiànzài bā diǎn bàn le, xuéshengmen yǐjīng kāishǐ shàngkè le.
examples.english: It’s eight thirty now, and the students have already started class.

entries.pos_note: Aspect particle after verbs and sentence-final particle are related but different uses.

examples.note: 很 + 冷 describes cold weather; context supplies how cold it feels.
examples.english: It is cold today.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 冷 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: It is colder tonight than it was this morning.

examples.note: 里 is a location word, showing that the book is inside the bag.
examples.english: The book is in the bag.

examples.note: School or study context showing 里 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students are having class in the classroom.

entries.pos_note: Localizer meaning inside, traditionally also categorized as a location noun.

examples.note: 两 is used before 个 and other classifiers to mean “two.”
examples.english: I have two children.

examples.note: School or study context showing 两 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào yǒu liǎng gè dà jiàoshì.
examples.english: The school has two large classrooms.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.english: It is midnight.

examples.hanzi: 学校有一百零二个学生。
examples.note: School or study context showing 零 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào yǒu yì bǎi líng èr gè xuéshēng.
examples.english: The school has one hundred and two students.

examples.note: 六 is a cardinal number used before the book classifier 本.
examples.english: I have six books.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 六 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: We are going to the bookstore on Saturday.

examples.note: 妈妈 can be used directly before a description without a possessive 的.
examples.english: My mother is a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈每天晚上和我一起读书。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 妈妈 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: māma měitiān wǎnshang hé wǒ yìqǐ dúshū.
examples.english: Mom reads with me every evening.

examples.note: Sentence-final 吗 turns a statement into a yes–no question.
examples.english: Do you like tea?

examples.note: School or study context showing 吗 in a simple description.
examples.english: Do we have class today?

entries.pos_note: Yes–no question particle.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.english: I want to buy some tea.

examples.note: School or study context showing 买 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéshēng kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ mǎi shū.
examples.english: Students can buy books here.

examples.note: 卖 is “sell,” in contrast to 买 “buy.”
examples.english: This shop sells fruit.

examples.hanzi: 学校外边的商店也卖书。
examples.note: School or study context showing 卖 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào wàibian de shāngdiàn yě mài shū.
examples.english: The shop outside the school also sells books.

examples.note: 忙 is a state adjective; 很忙 is a natural predicate without 是.
examples.english: I am very busy today.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈早上很忙，晚上有时间。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 忙 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: māma zǎoshang hěn máng, wǎnshang yǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: Mom is very busy in the morning but has time in the evening.

examples.note: 只 is the common animal classifier when counting cats.
examples.english: I have a cat.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 猫 in context.
examples.english: This cat likes sleeping.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: méi guānxi, wǒmen zài lái yí cì.
examples.english: It's okay; let's do it one more time.

examples.note: Written dialogue: 没关系 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.pinyin: “méi guānxi, wǒmen míngtiān zài lái.” tā shuō.
examples.english: "It's okay; we can come back tomorrow," she said.

entries.pos_note: Fixed reply meaning it is all right/it does not matter.

examples.note: 没事 is conversational reassurance, meaning that nothing is wrong.
examples.english: No problem, I am fine.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: “méishì, nǐ kěyǐ huí jiā.” tā shuō.
examples.english: "It’s okay; you can go home," he said.

entries.pos_note: Fixed reassurance meaning nothing is wrong/no problem; other verbal uses exist.

examples.note: 没有 expresses non-possession; it is not combined with 不.
examples.english: I don't have a mobile phone.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 没有 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: There is no class this afternoon.

entries.pos_note: Verb expressing absence or non-possession (我没有手机); negative adverbial 没(有) before a verb expresses nonoccurrence (我没有去). Both roles are kept, but the current examples illustrate non-possession/absence.

examples.note: 妹妹 refers to one’s younger sister and is a familiar family term.
examples.english: My younger sister is a student.

examples.hanzi: 妹妹每天和姐姐一起上学。
examples.note: Family or daily-life description using 妹妹 without advanced grammar.
examples.pinyin: mèimei měitiān hé jiějie yìqǐ shàngxué.
examples.english: The younger sister goes to school with her older sister every day.

examples.note: 们 marks a plural group of people in pronouns such as 他们, but is not freely added to every noun.
examples.english: They are all teachers.

examples.note: School or study context showing 们 in a simple description.
examples.english: The teachers are having class.

entries.pos_note: Plural suffix for personal pronouns and people nouns.

examples.note: 米饭 usually means cooked rice, not raw rice.
examples.english: I eat rice at noon.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 米饭.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā fàndiàn zhōngwǔ yǒu mǐfàn.
examples.english: This restaurant serves rice at lunchtime.

examples.note: 面包 means bread; 早饭 places the action at breakfast.
examples.english: I eat bread for breakfast.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 面包.
examples.english: There is bread and milk for breakfast.

examples.note: 面条儿 contains a northern 儿 ending; 面条 is also widely used.
examples.english: I want to eat noodles.

examples.note: This example uses the written form without the erhua ending.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā diàn de miàntiáo hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The noodles at this shop are delicious.

examples.note: 明年 places the trip next year; Chinese verbs do not change for future tense.
examples.english: Next year I will go to China.

examples.hanzi: 明年学校有新的汉语课。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 明年 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: míngnián xuéxiào yǒu xīn de Hànyǔ kè.
examples.english: The school will have new Chinese-language classes next year.

examples.note: 明天 sets the time for a planned future action.
examples.english: Tomorrow we are going to school.

examples.hanzi: 明天上午八点开始上课。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 明天 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: míngtiān shàngwǔ bā diǎn kāishǐ shàngkè.
examples.english: Class starts at eight tomorrow morning.

examples.note: 你的名字是什么 is a direct question about someone’s name; 叫什么名字 is another common wording.
examples.english: What is your name?

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 名字; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.english: Please write your name here.

examples.note: 哪 selects one among known choices; 本 is the measure word for books.
examples.english: Which book do you like?

examples.hanzi: 老师问：“你们想读哪本书？”
examples.note: The question word comes before the book classifier.
examples.pinyin: lǎoshī wèn: “nǐmen xiǎng dú nǎ běn shū?”
examples.english: The teacher asked, “Which book would you like to read?”

examples.note: 哪个 asks which one; 个 stands for the classifier of the implied object.
examples.english: Which one do you want?

examples.note: School or study context showing 哪个 in a simple description.
examples.english: Which student didn't come today?

examples.note: 哪里 asks where an institution or object is located.
examples.english: Where is the school?

examples.note: Written dialogue: 哪里 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: "Excuse me, where is the bookstore?" she asked.

examples.note: 哪儿 means where, with the 儿 pronunciation typical of northern Mandarin.
examples.english: Where are you going?

examples.note: Written dialogue: 哪儿 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: "Where is the school?" he asked.

examples.note: 哪些 means which ones when choosing several items.
examples.english: Which books do you like?

examples.note: School or study context showing 哪些 in a simple description.
examples.english: Which students can speak Chinese?

examples.note: 那 points to something away from the speaker, in contrast to 这.
examples.english: That is my friend.

examples.note: School or study context showing 那 in a simple description.
examples.english: That is the school's car.

entries.pos_note: Demonstrative pronoun; can also have discourse-connecting uses.

examples.note: 那边 denotes a place over there, away from the speaker.
examples.english: The store is over there.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 那边.
examples.english: There is a restaurant over there.

examples.note: 那个 identifies a particular item; 个 is its classifier.
examples.english: That apple is big.

examples.note: School or study context showing 那个 in a simple description.
examples.english: That student can speak Chinese.

examples.note: 那里 means “there” and is a full location word.
examples.english: My school is there.

examples.note: School or study context showing 那里 in a simple description.
examples.english: There are many students there.

examples.note: 那儿 is a northern-style alternative to 那里 for “there.”
examples.english: Are you going there?

examples.note: The quoted speaker uses the erhua form for “there.”
examples.pinyin: “qǐng zài nàr děng lǎoshī.” tā shuō.
examples.english: “Please wait for the teacher over there,” she said.

examples.note: 那些 points to several items away from the speaker.
examples.english: Those books are mine.

examples.note: School or study context showing 那些 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: nàxiē xuéshēng dōu zài jiàoshì lǐ.
examples.english: Those students are all in the classroom.

examples.hanzi: 那个男学生是我的朋友。
examples.note: 男 is an adjective specifying a male student; more formal contexts may use 男性.
examples.pinyin: nàge nán xuéshēng shì wǒ de péngyou.
examples.english: That male student is my friend.

examples.note: School or study context showing 男 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhège bān yǒu shí gè nán xuéshēng.
examples.english: There are ten male students in this class.

examples.note: 男朋友 ordinarily means boyfriend, not merely a male friend.
examples.english: Her boyfriend is a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 她的男朋友在医院上班。
examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: tā de nánpéngyou zài yīyuàn shàngbān.
examples.english: Her boyfriend works at a hospital.

examples.note: 你呢? is a compact way to return a question to the other person.
examples.english: And you?

examples.note: Written dialogue: 呢 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.pinyin: “wǒ huì shuō Hànyǔ, nǐ ne?” tā wèn.
examples.english: "I can speak Chinese. What about you?" she asked.

entries.pos_note: Sentence-final particle for follow-up, topic continuation, or ongoing action.

examples.note: 能…吗 can ask whether something is possible or permitted, here entering a room.
examples.english: May I come in?

examples.hanzi: 学生们在这里能看书，也能学习。
examples.note: The repeated modal links two activities students can do in this location.
examples.pinyin: xuéshengmen zài zhèlǐ néng kàn shū, yě néng xuéxí.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: nǐ hǎo, nǐ shì xīn xuéshēng ma?
examples.english: Hello, are you a new student?

examples.english: Hello! Nice to meet you.

examples.english: "Hello, excuse me, is anyone here?" she asked.

examples.english: The teacher said, “Come to class tomorrow at nine in the morning.”

examples.pinyin: wǒmen zài zhèlǐ zhù le liǎng nián.

examples.hanzi: 您好，请问您叫什么名字？
examples.note: 您 is the respectful form of 你, useful when addressing an unfamiliar adult.

examples.english: Hello, may I ask your name?

examples.note: The respectful form of “you” is part of the greeting.

examples.note: 每天 marks a daily routine; 喝牛奶 is a common verb-object phrase.
examples.english: I drink milk every day.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 牛奶.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 女朋友 in context.
examples.pinyin: tā de nǚpéngyou yě zài zhè jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: His girlfriend also works at this company.

examples.note: 女士 is a respectful label for an adult woman, more formal than 女人.
examples.english: This lady is a teacher.

examples.note: School or study context showing 女士 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: nà wèi nǚshì huì shuō Hànyǔ.
examples.english: That lady can speak Chinese.

examples.note: 好朋友 means a good or close friend, not a romantic partner.
examples.pinyin: tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: He is my good friend.

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友住在学校旁边。
examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: wǒ de péngyou zhù zài xuéxiào pángbiān.
examples.english: My friend lives next to the school.

examples.note: 便宜 describes a low price; it is not the same as bad quality.
examples.english: This apple is cheap.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 便宜.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā diàn de yīfu hěn piányi.
examples.english: The clothes at this shop are very cheap.

examples.note: 漂亮 describes attractive appearance, here that of clothing.
examples.english: This item of clothing is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 学校里有很多漂亮的花。
examples.note: School or study context showing 漂亮 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào lǐ yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de huā.
examples.english: There are many beautiful flowers at the school.

examples.note: 一个苹果 counts one apple; 每天 makes the action habitual.
examples.pinyin: wǒ měitiān chī yí ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: I eat an apple every day.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 苹果 in context.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā diàn de píngguǒ hěn piányi.
examples.english: The apples at this shop are very cheap.

examples.note: 七 is the quantity, followed by the general classifier 个.
examples.english: I have seven cups.

examples.note: School or study context showing 七 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: qī gè xuéshēng zài jiàoshì lǐ.
examples.english: Seven students are in the classroom.

examples.english: I get up at seven in the morning.

examples.hanzi: 学生们每天早上七点起床，八点上课。
examples.note: The two time expressions describe a daily routine.
examples.pinyin: xuéshengmen měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng, bā diǎn shàngkè.
examples.english: The students get up at seven and start class at eight every morning.

examples.note: 千 means a thousand; 一 is pronounced yì before qiān.
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ yǒu yì qiān běn shū.
examples.english: There are one thousand books here.

examples.hanzi: 这个学校有一千个学生。
examples.note: School or study context showing 千 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhège xuéxiào yǒu yì qiān gè xuéshēng.
examples.english: This school has one thousand students.

examples.note: 没有钱 expresses the absence of money; 不有 is not grammatical here.

examples.note: Straightforward statement of where an amount of money is located.
examples.pinyin: zhuōzi shàng yǒu èr shí kuài qián.
examples.english: There are twenty yuan on the table.

examples.note: 请坐 is a concise polite invitation to take a seat.
examples.english: Please sit down.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 请; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.english: Please sit here for a moment.

entries.pos_note: Polite request/please, grammaticalized use of the verb invite/ask.

examples.note: Written dialogue: 请问 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: "Excuse me, where is the cinema?" she asked.

examples.note: 去 indicates movement away from the speaker’s present location.
examples.english: We are going to school now.

examples.note: School or study context showing 去 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students will go to the cinema tomorrow.

examples.note: 去年 is last year; the sentence reports a past location without verb inflection.
examples.english: Last year I was in China.

examples.pinyin: qùnián wǒ zài zhège xuéxiào xuéxí.
examples.english: I studied at this school last year.

examples.note: 太热了 expresses more heat than desired or expected.
examples.english: It is too hot today.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 热 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The weather is very hot in the afternoon.

examples.note: 人 means a person; 一个好人 is one good person, with 个 as the classifier.

examples.english: He is a good person.

examples.pinyin: zhè jiā fàndiàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō rén.
examples.english: There are many people in this restaurant.

examples.english: I know this teacher.

examples.hanzi: 学生们都认识这个老师。
examples.note: School or study context showing 认识 in a simple description.
examples.english: All the students know this teacher.

examples.note: A polite question gives the date in a more formal style.
examples.pinyin: qǐngwèn, jīntiān shì shí yuè shísì rì ma?
examples.english: Excuse me, is today October 14?

examples.english: Today is May 1.

entries.pos_note: Day/date word; also a measure word for dates.

examples.note: 三 gives the count; 个 is the classifier for 朋友.
examples.english: I have three friends.

examples.note: School or study context showing 三 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: sān gè xuéshēng zài kàn shū.
examples.english: Three students are reading.

examples.english: We go to the store to buy water.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 商店 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The shop opens at nine in the morning.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: zhuōzi shàng yǒu liǎng ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: There are two apples on the table.

entries.pos_note: On/above as a localizer or verb for ascending/attending, depending on context.

examples.note: 上班 means go to work or start work, not simply enter a building.
examples.pinyin: wǒ bàba měitiān bā diǎn shàngbān.
examples.english: My dad goes to work at eight every day.

examples.hanzi: 很多人每天早上八点上班。
examples.note: The time phrase states when the workday starts.
examples.pinyin: hěn duō rén měitiān zǎoshang bā diǎn shàngbān.
examples.english: Many people start work at eight every morning.

examples.note: 上课 means start or attend class; the time gives when it begins.
examples.english: We start class at nine.

examples.hanzi: 学生们每天上午九点上课。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 上课 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: xuéshēngmen měitiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn shàngkè.
examples.english: The students have class at nine every morning.

examples.english: I have time in the morning.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 上午 in a straightforward sentence.

examples.note: 很少 describes a small number of people at this location.

examples.pinyin: jīntiān lái shàngkè de xuéshēng hěn shǎo.

examples.note: Written dialogue: 什么 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: "What do you want to drink?" she asked.

examples.note: 生病了 describes a change to an ill state; 昨天 puts it in the past.
examples.english: I became ill yesterday.

examples.english: She was sick yesterday and didn't go to class.

examples.note: 十 counts the books; 本 is the required classifier.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 十 in a straightforward sentence.

examples.note: 什么时候 asks when an event will happen, not merely for the clock time.
examples.english: When will you come?

examples.pinyin: shàngkè shíjiān shì shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn.
examples.english: Class starts at nine in the morning.

examples.note: 件 can count matters or incidents; 事 means a matter or thing to discuss.

examples.pinyin: shàngkè de shíhou qǐng búyào shuōhuà.
examples.english: Please don't talk during class.

examples.english: I read at home in the evening.

examples.hanzi: 晚上八点我们在家看电视。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 晚上 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: wǎnshang bā diǎn wǒmen zài jiā kàn diànshì.
examples.english: We watch TV at home at eight in the evening.

examples.note: 喂 is used to answer the telephone and is commonly pronounced wéi in that context, though wèi is also listed.
examples.english: Hello!

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: “wéi, nǐ hǎo, wǒ xiǎng zhǎo lǎoshī.” tā shuō.
examples.english: "Hello, I’d like to speak to the teacher," she said.

entries.pos_note: Attention-getting interjection; phone usage may be wéi or wèi depending on context.

examples.note: 问 introduces a question; 一个问题 is “one question.”
examples.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng wèn yí ge wèntí.
examples.english: I want to ask a question.

examples.note: School or study context showing 问 in a simple description.
examples.english: You can ask the teacher after class.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 问题 in context.
examples.english: I have a question.

examples.note: School or study context showing 问题 in a simple description.
examples.english: If you have questions, you can ask the teacher.

examples.note: 我 is the first-person singular pronoun; the sentence states a personal preference.
examples.english: I like Chinese.

examples.hanzi: “我每天上午在学校学习汉语。”她说。
examples.note: The first-person pronoun refers to the quoted speaker.
examples.pinyin: “wǒ měitiān shàngwǔ zài xuéxiào xuéxí hànyǔ.” tā shuō.
examples.english: “I study Chinese at school every morning,” she said.

examples.note: 我们 is “we”; 一起 emphasizes acting as a group.
examples.english: We study together.

examples.hanzi: 去年，我们一起在这个学校学习。
examples.note: The opening time word places this first-person account in the past.
examples.pinyin: qùnián, wǒmen yìqǐ zài zhè ge xuéxiào xuéxí.
examples.english: Last year, we studied together at this school.

examples.note: 五 gives the number, and 个 is the general classifier for apples.
examples.english: I have five apples.

examples.hanzi: 今天有五个学生没有来。
examples.note: School or study context showing 五 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: jīntiān yǒu wǔ gè xuéshēng méiyǒu lái.
examples.english: Five students did not come today.

examples.note: 午饭 means lunch, usually eaten around the middle of the day.
examples.english: We eat lunch at twelve.

examples.hanzi: 学生中午十二点吃午饭。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 午饭 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: xuéshēng zhōngwǔ shí èr diǎn chī wǔfàn.
examples.english: The students eat lunch at twelve noon.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 喜欢 in context.
examples.english: I like it here.

examples.note: Family or daily-life description using 喜欢 without advanced grammar.
examples.pinyin: hěn duō háizi xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: Many children like watching movies.

examples.note: 下面 is the full location expression below the table; 在 marks location.
examples.english: The cat is under the table.

examples.note: The target word appears in the location word for “under.”
examples.english: The book is under the chair.

entries.pos_note: Below/under as a localizer, but verb and measure-word uses also exist.

examples.note: 下雨 is the verb expression for rain; 了 can mark a new or completed event.
examples.english: It rained today.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 下雨; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.pinyin: xià yǔ de shíhou búyào chūqu.
examples.english: Don't go outside when it rains.

examples.note: 下班 means finish the workday or leave work, here at six.
examples.english: My father finishes work at six.

examples.hanzi: 下班后，我们去饭店吃饭。
examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 下班.
examples.pinyin: xiàbān hòu, wǒmen qù fàndiàn chī fàn.
examples.english: After work, we go to a restaurant to eat.

examples.note: 下课 means class has ended or is dismissed, here at four.
examples.english: We finish class at four.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 下课.
examples.english: After class, we go to the supermarket.

examples.note: 下午 is the period after noon; context can make the planned visit future.
examples.english: I will go to the store this afternoon.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 下午 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: xiàwǔ de kè sān diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.english: The afternoon class starts at three.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.english: This gentleman is a doctor.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: nà wèi xiānsheng zài xuéxiào gōngzuò.
examples.english: That gentleman works at the school.

examples.note: 上午十点 is 10 a.m.; 现在 gives the current time frame.
examples.english: It is ten in the morning now.

examples.note: School or study context showing 现在 in a simple description.
examples.english: Class starts now.

entries.pos_note: Temporal noun meaning now, not a verb.

examples.note: 想 indicates desire or intention; 学汉语 means learn Chinese.
examples.english: I want to learn Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 我妈妈想买一件新衣服。
examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 想.
examples.pinyin: wǒ māma xiǎng mǎi yí jiàn xīn yīfu.
examples.english: My mom wants to buy a new item of clothing.

entries.pos_note: Modal sense want/would like, also lexical verb think/miss.

examples.note: 只 is the animal classifier; 小 describes the cat’s size.
examples.english: This cat is very small.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 小 in context.
examples.english: This room is very small.

examples.note: 小朋友 is a friendly way to refer to young children.
examples.english: These children are playing.

examples.hanzi: 小朋友们每天上午在学校学习。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 小朋友 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: xiǎopéngyoumen měitiān shàngwǔ zài xuéxiào xuéxí.
examples.english: The children study at school every morning.

examples.note: 小时 expresses duration in hours; 两个小时 means two hours.
examples.pinyin: wǒ měitiān xuéxí liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I study for two hours every day.

examples.hanzi: 下午我们要上两个小时的课。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 小时 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: xiàwǔ wǒmen yào shàng liǎng gè xiǎoshí de kè.
examples.english: We have two hours of class in the afternoon.

examples.note: 上小学 refers to attending elementary or primary school.
examples.english: My child attends primary school.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 小学 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: Primary school classes start at eight in the morning.

examples.note: 小学生 specifies a primary-school pupil, not a college student.
examples.english: He is a primary school pupil.

examples.note: School or study context showing 小学生 in a simple description.
examples.english: These primary school students are having class.

examples.note: 些 expresses an unspecified plural amount, here some fruit.
examples.english: I would like to buy some fruit.

examples.hanzi: 这里有些书，也有些电脑。
examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 些 in context.
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ yǒuxiē shū, yě yǒuxiē diànnǎo.
examples.english: There are some books here, as well as some computers.

entries.pos_note: Indefinite quantity word, conventionally classified as a classifier/quantifier.

examples.note: 写 refers to writing a character; 会 indicates learned ability.
examples.english: I can write this character.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 写; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.english: Please write your name.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 谢谢 in context.
examples.english: Thank you for helping me!

examples.note: Written dialogue: 谢谢 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.english: "Thank you, teacher!" the student said.

examples.note: 新 modifies 书 to mean a new book.
examples.pinyin: zhè shì wǒ de xīn shū.
examples.english: This is my new book.

examples.note: School or study context showing 新 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā shūdiàn yǒu hěn duō xīn shū.
examples.english: This bookstore has many new books.

examples.note: 星期三 is Wednesday; weekdays are numbered from Monday as one.
examples.english: Today is Wednesday.

examples.hanzi: 这个星期有三天汉语课。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 星期 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: zhège xīngqī yǒu sān tiān Hànyǔ kè.
examples.english: We have Chinese classes on three days this week.

examples.note: 星期日 is a standard way to say Sunday; 星期天 has the same meaning.
examples.english: I rest on Sunday.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 星期日 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: The school has no classes on Sundays.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 星期天 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: We're going to the supermarket on Sunday.

examples.hanzi: 这个星期天我们去看电影。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 星期天 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: zhège xīngqītiān wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: We are going to watch a movie this Sunday.

examples.note: 休息 means rest or take a break, not necessarily go to sleep.
examples.english: I want to rest today.

examples.note: School or study context showing 休息 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students can rest after class.

examples.note: 学 focuses on learning a subject; 正在 marks an ongoing process.
examples.english: I am learning Chinese.

examples.note: School or study context showing 学 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students learn Chinese at school.

examples.note: 学生 is student in general; it does not by itself specify the school level.
examples.english: He is a student.

examples.note: School or study context showing 学生 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ yǒu èr shí gè xuéshēng.
examples.english: There are twenty students here.

examples.note: 学习 refers to studying or learning; 每天 makes it a repeated practice.
examples.english: I study Chinese every day.

examples.hanzi: 学生们每天在这里学习。
examples.note: School or study context showing 学习 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students study here every day.

examples.note: 学校 can refer to a school institution or its campus/buildings.
examples.english: Our school is big.

examples.note: School or study context showing 学校 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhège xuéxiào yǒu hěn duō lǎoshī.
examples.english: This school has many teachers.

examples.note: 地上有雪 states that there is snow on the ground, not merely that it is winter.
examples.english: There's snow on the ground.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 雪 in context.
examples.english: There's a lot of snow today.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.english: I want to drink water.

examples.hanzi: 上课的时候要听老师说话。
examples.note: School or study context showing 要 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: shàngkè de shíhou yào tīng lǎoshī shuōhuà.
examples.english: You must listen to the teacher during class.

entries.pos_note: Modal of intention/need, also a lexical verb meaning want.

examples.note: 也 means also; it normally appears before the verb or adjective predicate.
examples.english: I also like tea.

examples.hanzi: 学生也可以在这里看书。
examples.note: School or study context showing 也 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéshēng yě kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ kàn shū.
examples.english: Students can also read books here.

examples.note: 一 counts one older sister and changes to yí before neutral-tone 个.
examples.english: I have one older sister.

examples.note: 一 counts a single student with the measure word 个 in the common existential pattern 这里有… .
examples.english: There is one student here.

examples.note: 衣服 refers broadly to clothes; it commonly takes no classifier in this statement.
examples.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān mǎi le xīn yīfu.
examples.english: I bought new clothes today.

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 衣服.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā diàn mài hěn duō xīn yīfu.
examples.english: This shop sells many new clothes.

examples.note: 医生 is a doctor; 工作 describes their profession’s activity.
examples.english: Doctors work in hospitals.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 医生 in context.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā yīyuàn yǒu hěn duō yīshēng.
examples.english: This hospital has many doctors.

examples.note: 医院 means hospital; 去 expresses going to that destination.
examples.english: She goes to the hospital today.

examples.hanzi: 医院上午九点开始看病。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 医院 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: yīyuàn shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ kànbìng.
examples.english: The hospital starts seeing patients at nine in the morning.

examples.note: The apple is introduced as the topic; 一半 states that half was eaten.
examples.pinyin: zhège píngguǒ wǒ chī le yíbàn.
examples.english: I ate half of this apple.

examples.hanzi: 今天有一半的学生没有来上课。
examples.note: The fraction describes the share of students who missed class.
examples.pinyin: jīntiān yǒu yíbàn de xuésheng méiyǒu lái shàngkè.
examples.english: Half the students didn’t come to class today.

entries.pos_note: Fractional numeral phrase meaning one half.

examples.note: 等一下 is a polite request to wait a moment; 一下 softens the command.
examples.english: Please wait a moment.

examples.note: Written dialogue: 一下 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.pinyin: “qǐng kàn yíxià zhège zì.” lǎoshī shuō.
examples.english: "Please take a look at this character," the teacher said.

entries.pos_note: Verb-quantity complement meaning briefly/once; also adverbial in some uses.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 椅子; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.english: There are chairs here. Please sit down.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 椅子 in context.
examples.english: The chair is next to the table.

examples.note: 一点儿 means a little; the 儿 ending is written and pronounced in this form.
examples.english: I can speak a little Chinese.

examples.note: The quantity expression modifies water in a quoted request.
examples.pinyin: “qǐng gěi wǒ yìdiǎnr shuǐ.” tā shuō.
examples.english: “Please give me a little water,” he said.

entries.pos_note: Quantity expression a little, typically used in object phrases.

examples.note: 一些 means some or several; it precedes the noun 苹果.
examples.english: I bought some apples.

examples.note: School or study context showing 一些 in a simple description.
examples.english: There are some books in Chinese here.

entries.pos_note: Quantity expression some.

examples.note: 有 expresses possession; 两 is used before the classifier 本.
examples.english: I have two books.

examples.note: School or study context showing 有 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào lǐ yǒu hěn duō xuéshēng.
examples.english: There are many students at the school.

examples.note: 有的 before a noun means some members of a group, here some people.
examples.english: Some people like tea.

examples.hanzi: 有的学生喜欢唱歌，有的喜欢读书。
examples.note: School or study context showing 有的 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: yǒude xuéshēng xǐhuan chàng gē, yǒude xǐhuan dúshū.
examples.english: Some students like singing, while others like reading.

entries.pos_note: Indefinite/pronominal expression meaning some of a group (有的人、有的学生). The Level 1 grammar outline groups 有的 among demonstrative pronouns; it is not a degree adverb.

examples.note: 有点儿 often introduces a slight, sometimes undesirable, condition such as cold.
examples.english: It is a little cold today.

examples.hanzi: “这家饭店的菜有点儿贵。”她说。
examples.note: The degree adverb softens a mildly negative evaluation.
examples.pinyin: “zhè jiā fàndiàn de cài yǒudiǎnr guì.” tā shuō.
examples.english: “The food at this restaurant is a little expensive,” she said.

entries.pos_note: Degree adverb meaning a little; often conveys an undesirable degree.

examples.note: 有些 means some; here it modifies the group of students.
examples.english: Some students are absent.

examples.hanzi: 有些孩子今天没有来上学。
examples.note: Family or daily-life description using 有些 without advanced grammar.
examples.pinyin: yǒuxiē háizi jīntiān méiyǒu lái shàngxué.
examples.english: Some children didn't come to school today.

entries.pos_note: At beginner level, pronominal/determiner use means some or certain (有些学生). A secondary degree-adverb use means somewhat (有些冷), included as later-level usage.

examples.note: 雨很大 describes heavy rain; 大 can describe rain intensity.
examples.english: It's raining heavily today.

examples.hanzi: 昨天下午下了很大的雨。
examples.note: The adjective describes the intensity of the rain.
examples.pinyin: zuótiān xiàwǔ xià le hěn dà de yǔ.
examples.english: It rained heavily yesterday afternoon.

examples.note: The formal currency unit is used in a polite price question.
examples.pinyin: qǐngwèn, zhè ge bēizi shí yuán ma?
examples.english: Excuse me, is this cup ten yuan?

examples.note: The sentence states a price using the standard written currency unit.
examples.pinyin: zhè běn zhōngwén shū èrshí yuán.
examples.english: This Chinese-language book costs twenty yuan.

entries.pos_note: Currency unit yuan, functioning as a measure word.

examples.note: 下个月 means next month; no future-tense inflection is needed.
examples.pinyin: xià gè yuè wǒ qù Zhōngguó.
examples.english: I will go to China next month.

examples.note: Revised to exemplify the headword naturally using vocabulary from HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2.
examples.pinyin: míngnián wǔ yuè wǒmen qù Zhōngguó.
examples.english: We are going to China next May.

examples.note: 再 indicates repetition; 一次 is one occurrence, and 一 is pronounced yí before 次.
examples.english: Please say it again.

examples.note: Short everyday instruction or request using 再; the tone is polite or neutral.
examples.english: Please come back tomorrow.

examples.note: 在 + location states where the speaker is, not what they are doing.
examples.english: I am at home.

examples.note: School or study context showing 在 in a simple description.
examples.english: We have class at school.

entries.pos_note: Three common functions: verb of location (我在家), preposition/coverb introducing a place (我们在学校上课), and progressive adverb before a verb (我在看书). The first two are illustrated here; the primary lexicographic POS remains Verb.

examples.note: 再见 is the standard goodbye; 明天见 adds the expectation of meeting tomorrow.
examples.english: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!

examples.note: Written dialogue: 再见 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
examples.pinyin: “zàijiàn, xià ge xīngqī jiàn!” tā shuō.
examples.english: "Goodbye! See you next week!" she said.

entries.pos_note: Conventional farewell used as a fixed social expression; also analyzable as a verb.

examples.note: 来得很早 uses 得 to describe the manner or timing of arriving.
examples.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān lái de hěn zǎo.
examples.english: I came very early today.

examples.note: 很早 means early; this avoids repeating 早 in the same sentence.
examples.english: He gets up very early every day.

examples.note: 吃早饭 means have breakfast, and 七点 gives the time.
examples.english: I eat breakfast at seven.

examples.hanzi: 今天的早饭有包子和鸡蛋。
examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 早饭.
examples.pinyin: jīntiān de zǎofàn yǒu bāozi hé jīdàn.
examples.english: There are steamed buns and eggs for breakfast today.

examples.note: 早上 specifies the morning period; 喝茶 is the activity.
examples.english: I drink tea in the morning.

examples.hanzi: 我们每天早上八点上课。
examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 早上 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.pinyin: wǒmen měitiān zǎoshang bā diǎn shàngkè.
examples.english: We have class at eight every morning.

examples.note: 怎么写 asks how to write a particular Chinese character.
examples.english: How do you write this character?

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 怎么 in context.
examples.english: How do you do this question?

entries.pos_note: Interrogative pro-form meaning how, often adverbial in sentences.

examples.note: 你觉得怎么样 asks for someone’s impression or opinion.
examples.english: What do you think?

examples.note: The question word asks for an evaluation in quoted speech.
examples.pinyin: “zhè jiā fàndiàn de cài zěnmeyàng?” tā wèn.
examples.english: “How’s the food at this restaurant?” he asked.

entries.pos_note: Interrogative pro-form meaning how/how about; often adverbial in sentences.

examples.note: 在 + 找 signals a search that is currently in progress.
examples.pinyin: wǒ zài zhǎo wǒ de shǒujī.
examples.english: I am looking for my phone.

examples.note: School or study context showing 找 in a simple description.
examples.english: I'm going to the school to find the teacher.

examples.note: 这 means this; 这是什么 is a standard way to ask what something is.
examples.english: What is this?

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 这 in context.
examples.pinyin: zhè běn shū shì xīn de.
examples.english: This book is new.

examples.note: 请到这边来 invites someone to come over to this side.
examples.english: Please come this way.

examples.hanzi: 学校在这边，医院在那边。
examples.note: School or study context showing 这边 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào zài zhèbiān, yīyuàn zài nàbiān.
examples.english: The school is on this side, and the hospital is over there.

examples.note: 这个 means “this one,” with the noun inferred from context.
examples.english: This one is delicious.

examples.note: School or study context showing 这个 in a simple description.
examples.english: This student can speak Chinese.

examples.note: 这里 is a full location word meaning “here.”
examples.english: I live here.

examples.hanzi: 这里可以喝茶，也可以看书。
examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 这里.
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ kěyǐ hē chá, yě kěyǐ kàn shū.
examples.english: You can drink tea and read books here.

examples.note: 这儿 is a northern-style spoken alternative to 这里.
examples.english: Please come here.

examples.note: The quoted speaker uses the erhua form for “here.”
examples.pinyin: “zhèr yǒu yì jiā shūdiàn.” tā shuō.
examples.english: “There’s a bookstore here,” she said.

examples.note: 这些 means these plural items, here the apples.
examples.english: These apples are delicious.

examples.note: School or study context showing 这些 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhèxiē xuéshēng dōu zài xué Hànyǔ.
examples.english: These students are all learning Chinese.

examples.note: 真 adds strong, spontaneous positive emphasis to 好.
examples.english: The weather is really nice today!

examples.note: Practical shopping, food, or everyday-life context using 真.
examples.pinyin: zhè jiā fàndiàn de cài zhēn hǎochī!
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is really delicious!

entries.pos_note: Degree adverb truly/really, sometimes adjectival.

examples.note: 正在 makes the ongoing action explicit: reading right now.
examples.english: I am reading a book right now.

examples.note: School or study context showing 正在 in a simple description.
examples.english: The students are having class right now.

examples.note: 只 is the classifier for animals; here 两只猫 means two cats.
examples.english: There are two cats here.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 只 in context.
examples.english: That cat likes playing.

entries.pos_note: Classifier for animals and certain objects; not the adverb 只 (zhǐ) meaning only.

examples.note: 知道 means know a fact or piece of information, unlike 认识 for familiarity.
examples.english: I know your name.

examples.note: School or study context showing 知道 in a simple description.

examples.note: 中国 is the country China; 去 indicates travel to it.
examples.english: I want to go to China.

examples.note: School or study context showing 中国 in a simple description.
examples.english: There are many universities in China.

examples.note: 中文 refers to the Chinese language or writing; 会说 indicates speaking ability.
examples.english: I can speak Chinese.

examples.note: School or study context showing 中文 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ yǒu hěn duō Zhōngwén shū.
examples.english: There are many Chinese-language books here.

examples.note: 中午 means noon; 吃饭 can mean having lunch in this setting.

examples.pinyin: zhōngwǔ shí èr diǎn dào yì diǎn shì wǔfàn shíjiān.
examples.english: Lunch is from twelve to one.

examples.note: 中学 generally denotes secondary or middle school.
examples.english: My younger brother attends middle school.

examples.note: School or study context showing 中学 in a simple description.
examples.pinyin: zhège zhōngxué yǒu hěn duō lǎoshī.
examples.english: This middle school has many teachers.

examples.note: 中学生 is a secondary-school student, distinct from 小学生 and 大学生.
examples.english: She is a middle school student.

examples.note: Daily time or schedule context illustrating 中学生 in a straightforward sentence.
examples.english: Middle school students have class at eight in the morning.

examples.pinyin: xiànzài hěn duō xuéshēng zhù zài xuéxiào lǐ.
examples.english: Many students now live at school.

examples.note: 桌子上 means on the table; 有 introduces something located there.
examples.pinyin: zhuōzi shàng yǒu yì běn shū.

examples.note: Short beginner-level description illustrating 桌子 in context.

examples.english: There are many desks in the classroom.

examples.note: 怎么读 asks how to pronounce or read this written character.

changelog.changes: Applied a strict cumulative HSK 3.0 Levels 1–2 vocabulary ceiling for examples. Revised 24 example sentences in Level 1; removed words above Level 2, unlisted classifiers and proper names from those examples. Official headwords, IDs, other examples, classifications, and topic taxonomy unchanged. Kept the HSK 1 negative adverb 没 as a normal short form of 没有 where relevant.

Restored 300 English headword definitions from the original Excel; added tone-marked pinyin and English translations for all 600 current examples. Chinese sentences, IDs, categories, and POS unchanged. Original Excel transcriptions/translations reused for matching examples; revised/new examples enriched editorially.
Strict UTF-8 JSON re-export with independent syntax and structural validation. No vocabulary, pinyin, topic, POS, sentence, or example note changes from v1.5.1.

Reviewed the independent POS and topic facets against HSK 2025 grammar and vocabulary. Changed 边 to suffix-primary; assigned 事 to new Abstract & General Concepts topic (and added it as a secondary topic for 问题). Clarified POS notes for 半、多少、分、分钟、几、没有、有的、有些、在 and other ambiguous entries. Rejected mistaken proposals to tag 几 as a classifier, 有的 as an adverb, or 分 as noun-primary. Preserved all 300 IDs, headwords, pinyin, and 600 sentences without modification.

Reclassified all 300 vocabulary entries by independent semantic topics and grammatical parts of speech. Added controlled topic and POS taxonomies, primary and secondary tags, and usage notes for ambiguous functions. All 600 Chinese examples and existing IDs are unchanged.
Replaced the written second examples for IDs 226 (下) and 254 (一) with simpler, distinct Level 1 teaching sentences; revised their example notes. Other 598 sentences unchanged.

Replaced 295 difficult written examples and revised 18 conversational examples; simplified grammar and register for beginner study, followed by final naturalness edits. Existing IDs preserved; official 2025 ID remapping remains separate.
Introduced two examples per headword (conversational and written).

Taxonomy-only release: migrated from 20 to 22 top-level semantic topics (taxonomy v2.0.0), added 25 hierarchical subtopics and per-entry primary_subtopic_id/subtopic_ids. Reassigned selected primary/secondary topics; preserved all official IDs, headwords, pinyin, meanings, POS, and both example objects byte-for-byte at JSON value level. Source release 1.6.1.
Applied the 32-row register and naturalness patch to the v1.7.0 taxonomy release, revising 33 sentence examples and their annotations.

taxonomy.topic_policy: primary_topic_id is one active top-level parent; topic_ids begins with primary and permits meaningful secondary parents. primary_subtopic_id and subtopic_ids are optional for categories without subdivisions. All subtopic IDs must belong to parent topic_ids. Not official HSK categories.
taxonomy.pos_policy: primary_pos_id selects the most useful beginner lexical function, not an exclusive analysis; pos_ids includes independently documented secondary roles. Words like 几 (interrogative quantity) are not classifiers merely because they take classifiers after them. Secondary adverbial uses may be beyond beginner level; see pos_note.
